name: Start, Stop, Continue Retrospective
use_case: A team retrospective format that collects concrete behaviours under three headings — what we should start doing, what we should stop doing, and what is working and should continue — producing action items rather than a list of grievances. Best used at the end of a sprint, a project phase or a quarter, when the team wants to improve how it works together and needs a low-ceremony format that reliably converts discussion into named commitments.
strengths: the three prompts push contributions toward actions, not complaints
the Continue column protects practices that are quietly working
no preparation or materials needed beyond a shared surface
short enough to run every iteration without fatigue
weaknesses: surfaces symptoms; pair it with a root-cause method for recurring issues
becomes stale if run unchanged for many iterations in a row
quiet team members are easily drowned out without silent writing first
worthless if the Start items are never assigned an owner
